main_body: Three-storey brick townhouse facade with a slate mansard roof, two dormers, a chimney, a balcony band and a striped-awning shopfront
top_band: Light blue-grey roof-top band, rows 17-23 (L 95-122), closed by a dark edge row at 24 (L 53). Below it the slate slope runs from row 25 to 43, then an orange cornice at 44-46.
evidence: The roof shows a distinct top band (rows 17-23) with a lighter edge line at row 23 and a dark step at row 24. Below it a large slate slope with dormers reads as a visible roof surface, like the reference houses. The orange cornice (rows 44-46) and the dark row 47 under it act as an eave and shadow over the brick front face. Window frames, sills, the balcony and the awning stand out from the wall plane, so the front is not painted flat. The brick facade is mostly a vertical elevation, but the roof slope and top band make it a valid 3/4 building.

style.evidence: Shading and texture are good: the slate has about 5 steps with per-tile courses, the brick is mottled in several tones, and the windows carry warm glow dots. Flat-fill coverage is only 2%, and the median of 14 colours per tile is above house-h112 (11) and a little below house-h101 (18). The weak point is the outline. 97% of the dark edge pixels are neutral (#1d1722-type near-black), against 7-9% in both references, so the roof, dormer, chimney and facade edges read as a uniform black sticker line instead of the dark tone of the adjacent material. The palette is also small at 54 distinct colours, against 185 and 66 in the references. The near-black outline is the deciding failure.
